==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|sclise}}, {{m|enm|sklise}}, from {{der|en|fro|esclice}}, {{m|fro|esclis||a piece split off}}, deverbal of {{m|fro|esclicer}}, {{m|fro|esclicier||to splinter, split up}}, from {{der|en|frk|*slitjan||to split up}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*slitjaną}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*slītaną||to split, tear apart}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sleyd-||to rend, injure, crumble}}. Akin to {{cog|goh|sliz}}, {{m|goh|gisliz||a tear, rip}}, {{cog|goh|slīȥan||to tear}}, {{cog|ang|slītan||to split up}}, modern {{cog|fr|éclisse}}. More at [[slite]], [[slit]].

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/slaɪs/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-slice.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|en-au-slice.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-slice.wav}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪs|s=1}}

===Noun===
[[File:Kanapki z pomidorem.JPG|thumb|right|Slices of tomato and cheese (sense 2)]]
[[File:Giorgio's Pizzeria Slice of Pepperoni Pizza (29197647124).jpg|thumb|right|Slice of pizza (sense 4)]]
{{en-noun}}

# That which is [[thin]] and [[broad]].
#* {{RQ:Stevenson Treasure Island|text=I pulled in hand over hand on the cord, and when I judged myself near enough, rose at infinite risk to about half my height and thus commanded the roof and a '''slice''' of the interior of the cabin.}}
# A thin, broad piece cut off.
#: {{syn|en|cutting|snippet|Thesaurus:piece}}
#: {{ux|en|a '''slice''' of bacon; a '''slice''' of cheese; a '''slice''' of bread}}
#: {{ux|en|Jim was munching on a '''slice''' of toast.}}
# {{lb|en|colloquial}} An [[amount]] of anything.
#* {{quote-web
|en
|date=December 28, 2010
|author=Owen Phillips
|title=Sunderland 0 - 2 Blackpool
|work=BBC
|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/9317216.stm
|page=
|passage=Blackpool, chasing a seventh win in 17 league matches, simply could not contain Sunderland's rampant attack and had to resort to a combination of last-ditch defending, fine goalkeeping and a large '''slice''' of fortune.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724164201/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/9317216.stm|archivedate=24 July 2023}}
# A piece of [[pizza]], shaped like a [[sector]] of a circle.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2010|author=Andrea Renzoni; Eric Renzoni|title=Fuhgeddaboudit!|page=22
|passage=For breakfast, lunch, or dinner, the best Guido meal is a '''slice''' and a Coke.}}
# {{lb|en|British}} A [[snack]] consisting of [[pastry]] with [[savoury]] [[filling]].
#: {{ux|en|I bought a ham and cheese '''slice''' at the service station.}}
# A broad, thin piece of [[plaster]].
# A [[knife]] with a thin, broad blade for taking up or serving fish; also, a [[spatula]] for spreading anything, as paint or ink.
# A [[salver]], [[platter]], or [[tray]].
# A [[plate]] of iron with a handle, forming a kind of [[chisel]], or a spadelike implement, variously proportioned, and used for various purposes, as for stripping the planking from a vessel's side, for cutting blubber from a whale, or for stirring a fire of coals; a [[slice bar]]; a [[peel]]; a [[fire shovel]].
# One of the wedges by which the cradle and the ship are lifted clear of the building blocks to prepare for launching.
# {{lb|en|printing}} A removable sliding bottom to a [[galley]].
# {{lb|en|golf}} A shot that (for the right-handed player) curves unintentionally to the right. See {{m|en|fade}}, {{m|en|hook}}, {{m|en|draw}}.
#: {{syn|en|banana ball|banana slice}}
# {{lb|en|cricket}} A kind of [[cut]] [[shot]] where the [[bat]] makes an [[obtuse angle]] with the [[batter]].
# {{lb|en|Australia|NZ|UK}} Any of a class of heavy cakes or desserts made in a tray and cut out into squarish slices.
# {{lb|en|medicine}} A section of image taken of an internal organ using MRI (magnetic resonance imaging), CT (computed tomography), or various forms of x-ray.
# {{lb|en|falconry}} A [[hawk]]'s or [[falcon]]'s [[dropping]] which squirts at an angle other than vertical. (See [[mute]].)
# {{lb|en|programming}} A [[contiguous]] portion of an [[array]].

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cut into slices.
#: {{ux|en|'''Slice''' the cheese thinly.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cut with an edge using a drawing motion.
#: {{ux|en|The knife left '''sliced''' his arm.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|title=Prancer|lyricist=w:Greg Puciato|album=w:One of Us Is the Killer|artist=w:The Dillinger Escape Plan|date=12 March 2013|text=How could it all be / We've never been dead / But never awake from this dream / How could it all be / We've never been dead / Just mirrors running scared / '''Slicing''' wrists while we look for our own mortality / All the lights went out cold / Shadow covers the soul / Essence of the world made ceremonial / Now we all wait for the demise / What was the question? / Why do you need an answer? / You make me nauseous}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To clear (e.g. a fire, or the grate bars of a furnace) by means of a [[slice bar]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|badminton}} To hit the shuttlecock with the racket at an angle, causing it to move sideways and downwards.
# {{lb|en|transitive|golf}} To hit a shot that slices (travels from left to right for a right-handed player).
# {{lb|en|transitive|rowing}} To angle the blade so that it goes too deeply into the water when starting to take a stroke.
# {{lb|en|transitive|soccer}} To kick the ball so that it goes in an unintended direction, at too great an angle or too high.
# {{lb|en|transitive|tennis}} To hit the ball with a stroke that causes a spin, resulting in the ball swerving or staying low after a bounce.
